clue.text: Freshwater fish seen on river trip

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: An angler spots a fish during an outing on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A ride is a short journey or outing, so it is a synonym for a trip.

clue.text: Starts up again about energy saved in monetary figures

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: saved in says the energy letter is kept inside the monetary figures

parts.note: sums are amounts of money
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An economic recovery starts again, with energy savings reflected in the financial figures.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to begin again after a pause, matching starts up again.

clue.text: Shop selling various items -sort urged to diversify

indicators.note: to diversify is to make varied, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is urged to stock a wider variety of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An American drugstore sells medicines plus many sundries, so it is a shop selling various items.

clue.text: Nothing on before noon?. Ambassador will ring eminent people

indicators.note: will ring says the ambassador's letters encircle the rest

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
with all clothes off one has nothing on
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: Someone lounges unclothed all morning while an ambassador phones distinguished folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing on' means wearing nothing, all clothes off, not 'no event scheduled'. The odd '?.' is a print artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall of fame is, by extension, the whole group of celebrated or distinguished people in a field.

clue.text: Corroborate northward movement of soldiers before ordeal

indicators.note: in a down clue moving northward means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers
a test is a trying experience or ordeal

explanation.surface: A report of troops marching north before a hard trial needs confirming.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or confirm, a synonym of corroborate.

clue.text: Deliver carpet after short rest

indicators.note: after places the carpet word behind the next piece
short says the rest word loses its last letter

parts.note: to lie is to rest
to carpet someone is to reprimand them, to berate them

explanation.surface: A carpet is delivered after a brief nap.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is read in answer order: LI (LIE cut short) first, then BERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliver can mean set free, as in deliver us from evil, which is a synonym of liberate.

clue.text: Spooner's to follow mare that's bolted and pursue lost cause

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds are exchanged

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
a mare that has bolted is a horse that has fled, a fled horse

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to chase a runaway mare, a hopeless pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog a fled horse with D and FL swapped by sound gives the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means waste effort on something already settled or hopeless, just like pursuing a lost cause.

clue.text: Not all forensic images upset court advisers

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, reading them in reverse
not all of the words are used, so a run of letters is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Some forensic photographs have disturbed the experts advising a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' takes ICIMA from forensIC IMAges; 'upset' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Amici curiae, friends of the court, are impartial advisers offering legal expertise to a court.

clue.text: People risk both losing heads in lift

indicators.note: both losing heads says each of the two words drops its first letter

parts.note: men means people
a chance is a risk, as in take a chance

explanation.surface: People take a risk together, both getting decapitated in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN loses M and CHANCE loses C, leaving EN and HANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something can mean to improve or boost it, a synonym of enhance.

clue.text: Scouting's revival spiked by bit of sharp practice

indicators.note: spiked by means pierced by, so the second piece is put inside the first

parts.note: a renaissance is a revival
a con is a swindle, a piece of sharp practice

explanation.surface: The Scout movement's revival is marred by some dishonest dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scouting's' reads as 'Scouting is', with 'is' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance is military scouting: exploring an area to gather information.

clue.text: Trick taking in extremely dense pupil

indicators.note: taking in says the trick word holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: a stunt is a trick

indicators.note: extremely picks the outer letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A trick that fools a very slow-witted schoolchild.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is one being taught, the same as a student.

clue.text: Academic, very good one, stops rot

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so these letters sit inside the rot word

parts.note: bosh is nonsense, rot
OK is used to express approval
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A scholar, a decent sort, puts an end to some decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic as an adjective means scholarly, given to study and reading.

clue.text: What may be celebrated following study of everyday life

parts.note: a priest celebrates Mass
following something, watching it closely, is observation

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint at something celebrated, followed by a study of ordinary living.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass-Observation was a British social research project begun in 1937.
explanation.definitionFit: The project recorded daily life in Britain through volunteer diaries and observers, a study of everyday life.

clue.text: Retired private investigators' clubs

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: snoops are private detectives

explanation.surface: Former private detectives belong to certain clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoon was an old wooden golf club with a lofted face, so golf clubs.

clue.text: Put out article by European rebel

parts.note: the is the definite article
to rise is to rebel, as in rise up

explanation.surface: A rebel puts out an article for a European paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To etherise is to anaesthetise with ether, which puts a patient out, unconscious.

clue.text: Unconcerned about power one giant held

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about means going round, so the giant word surrounds the power letter

parts.note: massive means giant
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A giant seized by someone is oddly untroubled about power.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive means showing no emotion, calm and indifferent.

clue.text: "Train overdue" first of day-trippers scoffed

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the next word
to train is to shape or direct, so the following letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Day-trippers complain that their train is late.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed means ate up, gobbled.

clue.text: Where I worked on a couple of classical couplets

indicators.note: a couple of takes the first two letters of the next word
worked on means reshaped, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet recalls where they studied classical verse in rhyming pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a comic four-line biographical poem built of two rhyming couplets.

clue.text: Flowering plant, one in stock, a bloomer

parts.note: a cow is one of a farm's livestock
a bloomer is a blunder, a slip

explanation.surface: A garden plant kept in stock turns out to be a flowering one.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow-flowered wild primula.

clue.text: Government branch briefly put in as experts

indicators.note: put in says the department letters go inside the as letters

parts.note: dept is the short form of department, a branch of government

explanation.surface: A government department is briefly staffed as specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is someone highly skilled, so adepts are experts.

clue.text: Without risk securing worker for state capital

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the safe letters enclose the worker

parts.note: safe means without risk
an ant is a worker in crossword convention

explanation.surface: A worker is kept out of danger in a state's main city.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe is the capital city of the US state of New Mexico.

clue.text: Emperor imprisoning king in outskirts of town

indicators.note: imprisoning says the outer letters hold the king inside
outskirts of takes the outer letters of the next word

parts.note: a raja is an Indian king

explanation.surface: An emperor locks up a monarch on the edge of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman emperor of the second century AD.

clue.text: Why pa's notorious when drunk — it's a question of choice

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering about, so the letters of the phrase are jumbled

explanation.surface: Explaining why Dad's reputation suffers whenever he's had too much to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a jocular way of asking someone which drink they would like, inviting their choice.

clue.text: Mean to house old man quickly

indicators.note: to house means to contain, so the father letters sit inside

parts.note: mean in slang means excellent, as in a mean cook, so ace
pa is father, the old man

explanation.surface: A stingy person aims to accommodate an elderly man fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means at a swift pace, so quickly.

clue.text: 10, possibly, sides written about English composer

indicators.note: written about says the side letters are set round the others

parts.note: left and right sides give L and R
Thomas Arne was an English composer, of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A student composes music on both sides of a page about an English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 refers to 10-across, STUDENT; the stray 1 is a print artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is an example of someone still learning, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Short joke is going round about girl

indicators.note: short says the joke word loses its last letter

parts.note: a jest is a joke

indicators.note: going round turns the little word back on itself

parts.note: ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A brief joke is circulating about some girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessica is a female first name.

clue.text: Putting on a show before start of term — with resolution?

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the resolution of a story is its ending

explanation.surface: A school stages a show before term begins, hoping for a neat finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on a show can mean feigning, making a false display, a synonym of pretending.

clue.text: Honour death of speaker

indicators.note: of speaker says the word is as heard spoken by someone

parts.note: fate can mean death or destruction

explanation.surface: A speaker pays tribute to someone who has died.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour or celebrate them lavishly.
